 2 SCCH - 19  MVC.1452/2023  JUDGMENT The Petitioner filed this petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 claiming compensation from the respondent due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of Petitioner's case, are as under:
Munikrishna.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194358100/
1

sentences.text: On 27.11.2022 at about 11.30 a.m the Petitioner was traveling as a passenger in KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308 proceeding on Bangalore - Kolar NH-75 road, when the bus reached near Channapura gate, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, driver of the said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and unable to control over the same and dashed to road side divider.
As a result of forced impact, the bus was turtle and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to MVJ Hospital and undergone surgery, then shifted to Hosmat Hospital, wherein, he took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.1,30,000/- towards 3 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 medical expenses, transportation, conveyance and other charges.

4. It is contended that, this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308.
5.

It is contended that, prior to the accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was Working in a Hardware shop, at K.R.Market, and was earning Rs.19,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries he is not able to do his job and hence he had lost his earning and suffering from mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
Hence, prays to grant compensation.
6. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent appeared through it's Counsel and filed written statement.

7. Brief averments of the Written statement of Respondent are as under:
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition.

It is contended 4 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 that,
on the date of the accident, near Chennapura gate about 11-30 a.m. on Chennai National High way road, the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308 drove the same in a moderate speed, but the bus dragged to the side of the road and immediately the driver of said bus applied brake and tried to avoid the possible hitting of the bus on either side of the road, but the bus dragged beyond the control of driving and hit the road side divider, then it was stopped.
The bus had speed lock system.
It is contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the Petitioner.
It is contended that, the interim compensation has been paid to the Petitioner and that would be deducted at the time of passing the final award.

Further denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with costs.

5 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 Munikrishna.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194358100/
2 8.

On basis of the Pleadings and materials, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 27.11.2022 at about 11.30 p.m, When he was traveling in KSRTC bus bearing Reg No.KA-57/F-1308, on Bangalore-Kolar NH road,
near Channapura Gate, Hosakote, Bangalore Rural District, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed to the divider and jumped the divider after turtle the bus.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.
Whether order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case, Petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 08 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.

The driver of the Respondent bus got examined as Rw.1 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R1 to 4.
10.
Heard the arguments and Perused the materials available on record.

For the following reasons, I answer the above Issues as under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
REASONS 12. Issue No.1:-
The Petitioner filed this Petition for claiming compensation from the respondents due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

13. The Petitioner Sri.Munikrishna .M. got examined himself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and in his chief affidavit he had reiterated the averments of petition and got marked 08 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.

14. Ex.P1 is the Copy of F.I.R. Ex.P2 is the Copy of Complaint/Statement of witness, Ex.P3 is the Copy of Wound certificate, Ex.P4 is the Copy of Discharge summary, Ex.P5 Notarized copy of the Aadhaar card.
Ex.P6 is the Medical bills, Ex.P7 is the Prescriptions and Ex.P8 is the Charge sheet.

Munikrishna.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194358100/
3 7 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 15.
Sri.B.Mohan the driver of offending vehicle got examined as Rw.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination
and in his chief affidavit he had reiterated the averments of Written statement and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R1 to 4.
Ex.R1 is the Copy of Interim compensation payment receipt, Ex.R2 is the copy of ID Card, Ex.R3 is the Copy of D.L. and Ex.R4 is the Copy of Aadhaar card.

16. On perusal of Charge sheet it appears that, on Bangalore - Kolar NH-75 road, near Channapura gate, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, driver of the KSRTC Bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and lost control over the bus and dashed to the road side divider and caused the accident.
Hence, Hosakote Police filed Charge sheet against driver of the offending vehicle.

17. In the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the claimant has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble APEX 8 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The so-called reason that as the name of Dheeraj Kumar was not mentioned in the FIR, so it was not possible for Dheeraj Kumar to see the incident, is not a proper assessment of the fact- situation in this case.
It is well known that in a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Court must keep this distinction in mind.

10. Reference in this connection may be made to the decision of this Court in Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, in which the relevant observation on this point has been made and which is very pertinent and is quoted below:-
"

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."

18. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P1 - F.I.R. Ex.P2 - Complaint/Statement of witness, Ex.P3 - Wound certificate & Ex.P8 is the Charge sheet it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver 9 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308.
Hence, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:-
The Petitioner claimed the compensation amount of Rs.25,00,000/-.
As per Ex.3 Wound certificate the Petitioner sustained following injury:

Munikrishna.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194358100/
4
Left tibia shaft fracture (Open type -I)
The doctor opined that the above said injury is grievous in nature.

Therefore, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner and opinion of the doctor, I am of the opinion that, the Petitioner is entitled for amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
20. The Petitioner produced medical bills and hospital bills, which are marked as Ex.P6.
There is no any contradictions to disbelieve the bills produced by the Petitioner.

Hence, by considering the bills,
the Petitioner is entitled to claim the amount of Rs.1,65,000/- under the head of medical expenditure.
As per Ex.P4 discharge summary the Petitioner took treatment at Hosmat hospital from 27-11-2022 to 01-12-2022.
Sl.No.1 of Ex.P6 is Ambulance bill for a sum of Rs.2,000/-.
Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.8,000/- under the head Transportation, Nourishment and conveyance charges.
22. To prove the assessment of disability, the Petitioner had not examined his treated doctor to say about percentage of disability sustained by him.

23. The Learned Counsel for the Petitioner relied upon following citations in respect of compensation under the head future loss of income on account of permanent disability due to accidental injuries.

1. Civil Appeal No.4492/2023 In the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, (arising out of SLP (Civil)
No.138/2023 between Indra Bai V/s Oriental Ins.Co.ltd., & another.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. In the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru MFA.No.3721/2022(MV) C/w MFA.No.3583/2022(MV-I) 11 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 3.

In the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, Civil Appeal No.8598-8599 / 2022, between T.J.
Parameshwarappa @ Parameshwarappa @ J.T.Parameshwarappa @ Talalkena Gowdra Prameshwarappa V/s The New India Assurance Co. ltd.,
4. 2022 Live-law (SC) 1017 in the Hon'ble Supreme court of India, Civil Appeal No.9070- 9071/2022 (arising out of special leave Petition No.481-482-2019) .

entities.text:
T.J.
Parameshwarappa @ Parameshwarappa @ J.T.Parameshwarappa @ Talalkena Gowdra Prameshwarappa V/s The
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above said citations are not applicable to the case on hand, when the Petitioner had not examined his treated doctor and disability Certificate is not produced, then the question of granting the compensation under the head loss of future income on account of permanent disability does not arise.

Munikrishna.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194358100/
5 24.
The Petitioner was working in Hardware shop and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injury sustained by the Petitioner, this Tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.15,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period and loss of amenities.

Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount Pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000-00 Medical expenses Rs. 1,65,000-00 Towards Transportation, food, Rs. 8,000-00 nourishment, conveyance and other charges Towards loss of income during Rs. 15,000-00 laid up period and also towards amenities of life Total Rs. 2,18,000-00 The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,18,000/-.

26. Interest:
 For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for interest @6%
p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.

13 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 27. Liability:-
The Respondent is the RC Owner of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308.
As already discussed in the issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
28. The Respondent took contention that, already the interim compensation has been paid to the Petitioner and that would be deducted at the time of passing the final award.
Ex.R1 Interim Compensation payment receipt discloses that, the KSRTC authority had paid Rs.1,33,700/- to the Petitioner towards payment of interim compensation.
Further it is stated in the said receipt that, "in the event any compensation is awarded by the MACT, this amount is to be deducted from the awarded amount."

Therefore, out of total compensation amount, the interim compensation paid by the KSRTC should be deducted, which comes as follows:
Munikrishna.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194358100/
6 Rs.2,18,000/- - Rs.1,33,700/- = Rs.84,300/-.

entities.text: Munikrishna.M vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Here it is pertinent to note that at the time of accident, already the Respondent KSRTC authorities had paid amount of Rs.1,33,700/-
14 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 as interim compensation to the Petitioner and same is admitted by the Petitioner as per Ex.R1.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay only Rs.84,300/- to the Petitioner with interest.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Partly in the Affirmative.

29. Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.84,300/- (Rupees eighty four thousand and three hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further, Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 30 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner with proper verification and identification.
15 SCCH - 19 MVC.1452/2023 Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
